payload.section_heading: Section 2: Waiting Periods & Pre-Existing Diseases (PED) > 2.1 Standard Waiting Periods Schedule
payload.text:
[HDFC ERGO - Personal Optima Schedule | Section 2: Waiting Periods & Pre-Existing Diseases (PED) > 2.1 Standard Waiting Periods Schedule]
Clause 2.1.1 (Initial 30-Day Waiting Period - Code Excl03): Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within
30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising directly due to an
Accident.
Clause 2.1.2 (Specific Disease Waiting Period - Code Excl02): A 24-month continuous coverage waiting period
applies to specified illnesses and surgical procedures including Cataract, Benign Prostatic Hypertrophy, Hernia,
Hydrocele, Hysterectomy, Knee/Joint Replacement (non-accidental), Kidney Stones, and Gallbladder Stones.
Clause 2.1.3 (Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl01): Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease
(PED) such as Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension, Hypothyroidism, or Asthma and its direct complications shall be
excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy.
Clause 2.1.4 (Maternity Coverage Exclusion): Optima Secure does NOT cover Maternity or Childbirth expenses
under the base policy (except ectopic pregnancy which is covered under inpatient surgical treatment).

payload.section_heading: Chapter 1: Moratorium Period & Non-Contestability of Claims > 1.1 Reduction of Moratorium Period from 8 Years to 36 Months (5 Years to 3 Years)
payload.text:
[IRDAI Circular IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/05/2024 | Chapter 1: Moratorium Period & Non-Contestability of Claims > 1.1 Reduction of Moratorium Period from 8 Years to 36 Months (5 Years to 3 Years)]
Circular Reference: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/05/2024 | Effective Year: 2024 | Issued by: Insurance Regulatory and
Development Authority of India (IRDAI).
Clause 1.1 (36-Month Moratorium Rule): After completion of thirty-six (36) continuous months of coverage (3
years) under a health insurance policy across one or more insurers via portability, NO health insurance claim shall
be contestable by the Insurer on grounds of non-disclosure or misrepresentation of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED),
except in cases of proven established fraud.
Clause 1.2 (Maximum PED Waiting Period Cap): No health insurance product in India shall impose a Pre-Existing
Disease (PED) waiting period exceeding 36 months of continuous coverage.
Regulatory Provision Old IRDAI Rule New 2024 Master Circular Rule Legal Impact on Policyholder
Moratorium Period 60 Months (5 Years) 36 Months (3 Years) Insurer cannot reject claim for non-disclosure after 36M
Max PED Waiting Period 48 Months (4 Years) 36 Months (3 Years) All pre-existing diseases covered after 3 years
Free Look Period 15 Days 30 Days 100% refund of premium if cancelled within 30 days
Grace Period (Renewal) 15 Days (Monthly) 15 Days (Monthly) / 30 Days (Annual) Coverage continuity maintained during grace period

payload.section_heading: Chapter 2: Cashless Everywhere & Mandatory Turnaround Times (TAT) > 2.1 1-Hour Pre-Authorization & 3-Hour Discharge Mandate
payload.text:
[IRDAI Circular IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/05/2024 | Chapter 2: Cashless Everywhere & Mandatory Turnaround Times (TAT) > 2.1 1-Hour Pre-Authorization & 3-Hour Discharge Mandate]
Circular Reference: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/05/2024 | Topic: cashless_turnaround.
Clause 2.1 (1-Hour Cashless Authorization Rule): Every Insurer and Third Party Administrator (TPA) shall decide
on cashless pre-authorization requests immediately and strictly within ONE (1) HOUR of receipt of the request
from the hospital.
Clause 2.2 (3-Hour Final Discharge Rule): The Insurer shall grant final cashless discharge authorization within
THREE (3) HOURS of receiving the discharge request and final bill from the hospital. In no case shall the
policyholder be made to wait for discharge beyond 3 hours.
Clause 2.3 (Penalty for Delayed Discharge): If the Insurer delays discharge authorization beyond 3 hours, any
additional hospital bed/room charges levied by the hospital for the extended stay shall be borne strictly by the
Insurer from the Shareholders' Fund and NOT deducted from the Policyholder's Sum Insured.
Clause 2.4 (Death During Treatment): In the event of death of the insured patient during hospitalization, the insurer
shall immediately settle the claim request and ensure the mortal remains are released from the hospital without
delay.

Emergency Pre-Authorization Within 1 Hour (60 Mins) Escalation to GRO / Bima Bharosa Portal
Final Discharge Approval Within 3 Hours (180 Mins) Insurer must pay extra hospital detention/room charges
No-Claim Bonus / Discount Reward for Claim-Free Year Option to take increased SI or discount in renewal premium

payload.section_heading: Chapter 3: Grievance Redressal, Claim Rejection Rules & Insurance > 3.1 Ban on Arbitrary Claim Rejection & Ombudsman Escalation
payload.text:
[IRDAI Circular IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/05/2024 | Chapter 3: Grievance Redressal, Claim Rejection Rules & Insurance > 3.1 Ban on Arbitrary Claim Rejection & Ombudsman Escalation]
Circular Reference: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/05/2024 | Topic: grievance_redressal.
Clause 3.1 (No Claim Rejection Without Committee Approval): No claim shall be repudiated/rejected directly by a
TPA. Repudiation of any claim requires explicit approval from the Insurer's three-member Claims Review
Committee (CRC).
Clause 3.2 (No Rejection for Want of Documents): No claim shall be closed or rejected merely for want of
documents. Required documents must be called for at the time of admission itself.
Clause 3.3 (Insurance Ombudsman Award Compliance): If an insured escalates a complaint to the Insurance
Ombudsman (for claims up to Rs. 50 Lakhs) and an Ombudsman Award is passed in favor of the policyholder, the
Insurer MUST comply with the award within 30 days. Failure to comply attracts an unconditional penalty of Rs.
5,000 per day payable to the complainant, plus penal interest at 2% above the prevailing bank rate.
Clause 3.4 (Portability Rights): Policyholders may port their policy to another insurer at least 45 days before
renewal with 100% credit for served waiting periods and accumulated No-Claim Bonus.
